problem: The lesson splices in an unrelated topic — a whole teach slide on shades of certainty (knew/believed/suspected) that has nothing to do with literal vs. nonliteral meaning — making it incoherent and confusing for a kid trying to learn one skill

the lesson is incoherent: the example teaches using a new vocab word, but the tip and interactive abruptly switch to discourse markers (Oh/Well/So) that were never modeled, so the practiced skill doesn't match the taught skill

Contains real phonics errors that a reading specialist would reject: 'were has a silent E that helps it end in R' and 'have ends in a silent E' are nonsense explanations — these words are irregular precisely because they DON'T follow rules, yet the lesson invents fake rules for them, undercutting the whole point and teaching misinformation.
